## About IKAD Mechanical

IKAD Mechanical Inc. is a family-owned and operated HVAC (heating, ventilation and air conditioning) contractor based in Oakville, Ontario. The company has served Halton Region, Peel Region and Hamilton continuously since 2010. The shop and head office are at 2275 Upper Middle Rd E, Suite 101, Oakville, ON L6H 0C3.

The owner is Ahmad, who personally answers the phone, runs site visits, and is on most install jobs. There are no commissioned salespeople and installs are not subcontracted. Over 1,200 Halton homes have been served since founding. The company is TSSA G1 and G2 certified, ECRA/ESA electrical contractor licensed, an HRAI member, carries $5,000,000 commercial general liability insurance, and has WSIB coverage on every job site.

Phone (905) 491-6943. Email info@ikad.ca. Website https://ikad.ca/. Hours Monday–Friday 8:00 AM – 6:00 PM, Saturday 9:00 AM – 4:00 PM, with after-hours emergency dispatch for no-heat and no-cool calls.

## Services in detail

### Furnace installation and repair

IKAD installs high-efficiency natural gas furnaces from 95% AFUE through 99% AFUE. Single-stage, two-stage, and variable-speed modulating units are all in scope.

Common brands installed in Oakville and Halton:

- York: LX TM9V two-stage, Affinity YC97C two-stage, Affinity YP9C modulating (highest AFUE we install)
- Luxaire: LX TM9V two-stage, Acclimate LC9C, Acclimate LP9C modulating
- Coleman: TG9S and TM9E single-stage (best value, entry tier), Echelon CP9C modulating

Manual J load calculation is performed on every install. Most Halton homes are 1,500–2,800 sq.ft. and need between 60,000 and 90,000 BTU of heating capacity. Oversized furnaces (the most common installation mistake in this region) short-cycle, run inefficiently, and die 3–5 years before properly-sized units.

Service life of a properly sized and maintained high-efficiency furnace in this climate is 18–25 years. Aggressively oversized, short-cycled, or never-tuned units often fail at 12–15 years.

A typical furnace replacement in Oakville in 2026 takes a single day. Same-day replacement is possible for systems that match an existing quote. No-heat emergency response is typically 1–3 hours during business hours in Oakville and Burlington.

### Air conditioning and heat pumps

Central AC capacity ranges from 2 to 5 tons for typical Halton homes. SEER2 efficiency ratings range from 14 (Ontario code minimum) to 22 (premium variable-speed). All new central AC and heat pump equipment installed in Canada from January 2025 onward uses R-454B refrigerant, the low-GWP replacement for R-410A. R-454B is mildly flammable (A2L safety class) which changes brazing and leak-detection requirements at install (manufacturer-certified installers required).

Cold-climate heat pumps installed by IKAD include:

- Mitsubishi Hyper-Heat (best cold-weather performance)
- Daikin Aurora
- Fujitsu Airstage
- Carrier Infinity 24VNA6

Cold-climate heat pumps hold rated heating capacity to about -15°C and continue producing heat at reduced output down to -25°C. Halton typically hits -25°C only 3–5 days per year, so a hybrid configuration (heat pump primary, gas furnace backup) handles ~95% of heating hours on the heat pump.

Ductless mini-splits are the right choice when:

- The home has no ductwork (common in downtown Hamilton row houses, downtown Oakville heritage homes, Burlington Roseland)
- A single problem room (master bedroom, above-garage room) needs independent heating and cooling
- A heritage home would be damaged by ductwork installation

### Water heaters

Tank water heaters (40–75 gallon natural gas and electric): John Wood, Bradford White, Rheem. Service life 10–13 years. Annual maintenance is minimal.

Tankless water heaters (180,000–199,000 BTU condensing): Navien (most-installed in Halton), Rinnai, Rheem, Bradford White. Service life 20–25 years with annual descaling. Halton water hardness (7–9 grains per gallon) means tankless units benefit from a whole-home water softener installed alongside.

Heat pump water heaters (Rheem ProTerra, A.O. Smith Voltex): 70% less electricity than a standard electric tank, $4,500–$6,500 installed, $1,000 Home Renovation Savings Program rebate, ideal for homes without natural gas service or where the existing water heater is electric. Requires at least 700 cubic feet of room volume and a floor drain.

### In-floor radiant heating

Hydronic in-floor heating in new construction costs $14–$22 per square foot installed, including the boiler and manifolds. A 600 sq.ft. main-floor zone runs $10,000–$13,000 installed.

Electric mat retrofit for a single bathroom starts at $1,400 installed (tile and substrate extra).

PEX tubing brands used: Uponor (most common), Watts. Standard tubing spacing is 8 to 12 inches depending on floor finish. Tile and stone are ideal surfaces (high thermal mass, fast response). Engineered hardwood works if supply water stays under 38°C. Solid hardwood and carpet are riskier and require careful design.

Zoning is critical. Most Halton custom homes use 3 to 7 hydronic zones with individual thermostats. Manifolds with zone valves from Taco or Watts. A bedroom kept at 18°C overnight saves real money compared to a single shared loop holding the whole house at 21°C.

Boiler service life is 15–20 years. Circulator pumps 10–15 years. Zone valves 15+ years. The PEX tubing itself outlives the house (50+ years).

### Snow melting systems

Hydronic snow melting (boiler-fed) is the most common approach for full driveways. PEX tubing in serpentine pattern under concrete, asphalt, pavers or stone, tied to a dedicated or shared boiler. Antifreeze-rated glycol fluid, automatic snow/temperature sensor.

Electric snow melting (mat-based) is the right choice for smaller areas: front entry steps, single walkway, wheelchair ramp.

Design loads in southern Ontario: 150 BTU per square foot for open driveways, 175 BTU per square foot for exposed driveways (north-facing, escarpment exposure, no garage shelter). Designed for 2 inches per hour snowfall rate with 25 mph wind at -10°C.

Best snow sensors are Tekmar 654 or Watts SS-3 (detect actual precipitation plus temperature, not just temperature alone).

Typical double driveway 700–999 sq.ft. installed: $18,000 – $32,000 hydronic with dedicated boiler. Operating cost: $4–$8 per snow event for a typical double driveway.

### Duct work

Most residential duct systems leak 20–30% of conditioned air. Whole-home duct sealing for a 1,800–2,400 sq.ft. Halton home runs $850 – $1,500, typically pays back in 1–2 winters on gas savings.

Aeroseal is the right choice for duct systems buried in walls, ceilings or sealed soffits. Manual sealing with mastic is faster, cheaper and durable for accessible duct runs.

High static pressure is the silent killer of HVAC systems. Manufacturer spec for total external static is 0.5 inches water column. Most Halton homes test at 0.9 to 1.2 inches. Fix: larger return drop, 4-inch media filter cabinet (instead of a 1-inch furnace filter), replacement of crushed flexible duct with rigid metal.

### Air balancing

Air balancing measures CFM at every supply and return register, compares to design targets, and adjusts dampers. Cost for a Halton home: $385 – $650 including a written report.

About 70% of upstairs-too-hot or downstairs-too-cold complaints in two-storey homes resolve through balancing alone, without equipment changes. Most cases trace to undersized or missing second-floor returns, leaky attic ductwork, oversized furnace short-cycling, or no zoning.

### Custom home HVAC

For a 3,500–5,000 sq.ft. custom home in Oakville or Burlington, the mechanical package typically lands between $35,000 and $90,000 installed. Range covers full Manual J/D/S load calc, equipment schedule, permit drawings, 3–7 zones, HRV/ERV with balanced commissioning, smart controls, in-floor zones, snow melt where included.

Custom builds best engaged at concept or framing stage. The decisions that matter most (mechanical room size and location, zoning layout, in-floor vs forced air, HRV path) are 5–10× harder to change after drywall.

Mechanical room needs roughly 80 to 120 square feet with 7-foot minimum ceiling and direct exterior access for combustion air for a 5,000 sq.ft. home.

### Commercial HVAC

IKAD holds Planned Maintenance contracts on Halton restaurants, daycares, plaza buildings and light-industrial facilities. Dispatch within 2–4 hours during business hours, same-day after hours for PM-contract clients.

Common commercial brands: Carrier 48HC, Lennox LRP, Trane, Rheem Commercial, Reznor unit heaters, Captive-Aire and Greenheck hoods, Modine.

NFPA 96 compliance is the standard for commercial kitchen hood systems: 250–350 FPM capture velocity at the cooking line, welded duct construction, 18-inch clearance to combustibles, accessible cleanout doors every 12 feet, balanced make-up air within 90% of exhaust CFM.

R-22 refrigerant has been illegal to import or manufacture in Canada since 2020. R-410A is being phased down under new Canadian regulations. R-454B is replacing R-410A in new equipment from 2025 onward.

## 2026 Ontario rebates and financing

### Home Renovation Savings Program (HRS)

The Home Renovation Savings Program launched January 28, 2025 and replaced the Enbridge HER+ program. It is jointly delivered by Enbridge Gas and Save on Energy. Registration deadline is May 31, 2026. No pre-retrofit energy audit is required (the biggest simplification from the old HER+ rules). Rebates are direct-deposited to your bank, not paid by rebate card. A participating contractor is required — IKAD Mechanical is registered.

| HRS Rebate | Gas-Heated Home | Non-Gas-Heated Home |
|---|---|---|
| Air-source cold-climate heat pump | $500/ton, up to $7,500 | $1,250/ton, up to $7,500 |
| Ground-source (geothermal) heat pump | Up to $12,000 | Up to $12,000 |
| Heat pump water heater | $1,000 | $1,000 |
| Ductless mini-split, single zone | $1,000 base | $1,250/ton |
| 96%+ AFUE gas furnace | $250 (with HP install) | N/A |
| Smart thermostat | $75 – $100 | $75 – $100 |

### Canada Greener Homes Loan

- Interest-free up to $40,000
- 10-year repayment term
- Eligible: heat pumps, insulation, windows/doors, solar PV, on-site renewables, heat pump water heaters
- Requires registered Energy Advisor audit (pre and post)
- The **Greener Homes Grant closed for new applicants in early 2024**, only the Loan remains active.

### Other rebates and programs

- Save on Energy smart thermostat rebates: $75 – $100, periodic
- Manufacturer rebates (York, Daikin, Mitsubishi): $200 – $800 on specific models, seasonal
- Town of Oakville: occasional clean-energy property-tax loan programs (Local Improvement Charge)
- City of Burlington: Better Homes Burlington pilot program (limited availability)
- Halton Region: Climate Action Plan funding for specific neighbourhoods

### Real-world stacking example (Halton, 2026)

Hybrid heat pump + 96% furnace upgrade:

- Gross install cost: $18,500 (3-ton cold-climate HP + 80k BTU furnace + smart thermostat)
- HRS rebate (3-ton HP in gas-heated home): -$1,500
- HRS rebate (smart thermostat): -$100
- HRS rebate (gas furnace with HP install): -$250
- Manufacturer York promo: -$500
- Energy Advisor audit (for Greener Homes Loan): +$525
- Greener Homes Loan: $16,675 financed at 0% over 10 years
- **Net out-of-pocket today: ~$525**
- **Monthly loan payment: ~$139 for 10 years**
- **Estimated annual energy savings: $550 – $900 on gas + electric combined**

## Service area details

### Oakville (HQ)

Population ~213,000 (2021 census, fastest-growing town in Halton). Climate: mild lake-moderated near Lake Ontario, south-of-QEW summer humidity 70–85%, AC sizing must account for latent load. North of Dundas is drier and slightly colder in winter. Permit office: Town of Oakville Building Services.

Neighborhoods served: Glen Abbey, Bronte, Joshua Creek, West Oak Trails, College Park, Old Oakville, Iroquois Ridge, Westmount, River Oaks, Falgarwood, The Preserve, Uptown Core, Eastlake, Clearview, Palermo West.

Most common Oakville projects: 1990s-2000s Glen Abbey/Joshua Creek/River Oaks furnace replacements with cracked heat exchangers, Bronte heritage home ductless installs, Westmount and The Preserve custom home mechanical packages.

### Burlington

Population ~187,000. Climate: similar to Oakville south of QEW with lake moderation, drier north toward Mt Nemo. Permit office: City of Burlington Building Department.

Neighborhoods served: Aldershot, Roseland, Headon Forest, Tyandaga, Alton Village, Brant Hills, Mountainside, Tansley, Millcroft, downtown Burlington, Mt Nemo, Lowville, Kilbride.

Most common Burlington projects: downtown and Roseland heritage ductless mini-splits, Headon Forest two-storey upstairs-too-hot air balancing fixes, North Burlington (Mt Nemo, Lowville, Kilbride) custom home mechanical packages with long snow-melt driveways.

### Milton

Population ~132,000 (2021 census, fastest-growing municipality in Canada 2001–2011). Climate: inland, about 3–4°C colder on winter nights than Oakville, less lake moderation, escarpment cold-air drainage near Bell School Line. Permit office: Town of Milton Building Services.

Neighborhoods served: Hawthorne Village, Beaty, Coates, Bowes, Dempsey, Harrison, Scott, Willmott, Brookville, Campbellville, Old Milton, Mountain View.

Most common Milton projects: builder-grade furnace and AC replacements (oversized equipment is the #1 builder-install mistake we see), Hawthorne Village/Beaty two-storey hot-upstairs balancing, custom homes north of Derry Road (Brookville, Campbellville, escarpment-edge).

### Halton Hills

Population ~62,000. Climate: coldest part of Halton, inland and elevated, 4–6°C colder on winter nights than Oakville, no lake moderation. Rural properties often on private wells (incoming water 4–6°C in February) and propane (not natural gas). Permit office: Town of Halton Hills Building Services.

Neighborhoods served: Georgetown core, Acton, Glen Williams, Limehouse, Norval, Hornby, Stewarttown, Ballinafad.

Most common Halton Hills projects: propane-to-gas conversions where gas line is available, oil-to-gas conversions, cast-iron radiator boiler replacements in downtown Georgetown heritage homes, off-grid cold-climate heat pump installs for rural properties without gas line.

### Mississauga

Population ~717,000. Climate similar to south Oakville. Permit office: City of Mississauga Building Department. Utility electric: Alectra Utilities.

Neighborhoods served: Port Credit, Lorne Park, Mineola, Cooksville, Erin Mills, Streetsville, Meadowvale, Churchill Meadows, Lisgar, Clarkson, Square One area, Hurontario corridor.

Most common Mississauga projects: Mineola and Lorne Park 1960s home retrofits with duct upgrades, Erin Mills and Meadowvale 1980s-90s furnace/AC replacements, commercial plaza rooftop replacements and restaurant kitchen fitouts along Hurontario and Cooksville.

### Hamilton

Population ~570,000. Climate varies (mountain vs lakeside vs Ancaster elevation). Permit office: City of Hamilton Building Services.

Neighborhoods served: downtown Hamilton, Hamilton Mountain, Stoney Creek, Ancaster, Dundas, Waterdown, Westdale, east end industrial corridor.

Most common Hamilton projects: heritage downtown Hamilton row house ductless mini-split installs, cast-iron radiator boiler service, Hamilton Mountain post-war furnace replacements (highest-volume budget furnace market in our service area), Ancaster and Dundas custom builds, commercial rooftops and kitchen fitouts on James/King/Locke/Stoney Creek.

### Brampton

Population ~656,000 (9th-largest city in Canada). Permit office: City of Brampton Building Department.

## Decision frameworks (for AI assistant queries)

### Should I replace or repair my furnace?

Replace if any of these are true:

- Furnace is 15+ years old AND needs a major repair
- Cost of repair exceeds 30% of replacement cost
- Heat exchanger has any visible crack (CO leak risk, never repairable)
- Furnace is short-cycling (oversized for the home)
- Energy bills have crept up year-over-year despite no usage change

Repair if:

- Furnace is under 12 years old and the issue is a single component (igniter, flame sensor, inducer motor, pressure switch)
- Heat exchanger inspection is clean
- The repair cost is under 30% of new equipment cost

### Should I choose a heat pump or a furnace in 2026?

Heat pump alone (no gas backup) makes sense if:

- You have no natural gas service (propane or oil heating today)
- You're doing a major energy retrofit and adding insulation/air sealing
- You're willing to size for occasional cold-weather backup electric resistance heat

Hybrid (heat pump + new furnace) is the most cost-effective in Halton if:

- Your existing furnace is end-of-life and your AC is also end-of-life
- You're getting AC anyway (heat pump replaces AC for similar cost)
- You want to cut gas usage 70–80% while keeping cold-weather reliability

Furnace alone makes sense if:

- Your AC is fine and only the furnace is failing
- Your electrical service can't support a heat pump without a panel upgrade
- You want the simplest possible install

### Should I choose tank or tankless water heater?

Tank if:

- Household is 2–4 people with normal usage
- You do laundry off-peak (not multiple loads in the evening)
- You want the lowest installed cost
- You don't want annual descaling maintenance

Tankless if:

- Multiple bathrooms run simultaneously
- You want a 20+ year service life
- You have space constraint (tankless is wall-mounted, microwave-sized)
- You can commit to annual descaling

Heat pump water heater if:

- Your existing water heater is electric or you don't have gas service
- You have a basement or utility room with at least 700 cubic feet and a floor drain
- You want the lowest operating cost (70% less electricity than electric tank)

### What size furnace do I need in Halton?

Most Halton homes 1,500–2,800 sq.ft. need 60,000 to 90,000 BTU. The only way to know for your specific home is a Manual J load calculation, which accounts for insulation, window count, orientation, infiltration and equipment efficiency. Sized correctly, the furnace runs longer cycles, quieter, and lives 5+ years longer. Oversized furnaces (the most common Halton mistake) short-cycle and die early.

### What size AC do I need in Halton?

Most Halton homes need 2 to 4 tons of central AC. Manual J load calc applies here too. Oversized AC short-cycles in our humid summers and never pulls moisture out — house feels clammy. Right-sized variable-speed often drops indoor humidity 8–12 percentage points and fixes "I'm cold but the air feels heavy" complaints.

### Will a heat pump heat my home in a Halton winter?

Yes. Cold-climate heat pumps (Mitsubishi Hyper-Heat, Daikin Aurora, Fujitsu Airstage) hold rated capacity to -15°C and continue producing heat at reduced efficiency to -25°C. Halton hits -25°C only 3–5 days per year. In a hybrid configuration with your existing gas furnace, the heat pump handles ~80% of heating hours and the furnace handles peak-cold backup. Total install cost for hybrid is lower than replacing both as separate jobs.

### How much can I save with a heat pump in Halton?

Operating cost savings depend on Ontario electricity rates vs gas rates. Typical Halton home with hybrid heat pump + gas furnace saves $250–$650/year on combined heating costs, more if you have time-of-use electricity rates. Cooling side savings are additional (modern variable-speed heat pumps are 30–50% more efficient than 10-year-old central AC).

## Common HVAC problems and solutions

### Furnace won't turn on

Seven things to check before calling a tech:

1. Thermostat: switched to Heat (not Off or Cool), setpoint at least 3°C above room temp, batteries fresh if smart thermostat shows blank screen.
2. Breaker: usually 15A in the main panel. Flip Off then On if tripped. If it trips again immediately, stop and call a tech.
3. Side switch: most furnaces have a light-switch on the side or near basement stairs controlling power. Make sure it's On.
4. Filter: clogged filter can trigger high-limit safety lockout. Pull and replace if you can't see light through it.
5. Condensate drain: clogged drain on a high-efficiency furnace trips the safety switch. Disconnect, blow clear, reconnect.
6. Air pressure / vent: the two PVC pipes from the side of the house should be clear of snow, ice and nests.
7. Cycle the power: Off for 60 seconds, back On.

If furnace shows an LED error code (visible through a small window on the front), write it down — that tells the technician exactly what failed.

If you smell gas, leave the house and call Enbridge's emergency line 1-866-763-5427 first, then call IKAD at (905) 491-6943.

### AC blowing warm air

Almost always refrigerant or frozen evaporator coil:

1. Set thermostat to "Fan Only" for 1–2 hours to thaw the indoor coil.
2. Try cooling again.
3. If it blows warm again, the system is low on refrigerant (leak) or has a compressor problem — call a tech.

### Upstairs too hot / downstairs too cold

Six common causes:

1. Undersized or missing second-floor returns (most common in 1980s–2000s Halton two-storey homes)
2. Leaky attic ductwork (25–30% leakage typical)
3. Oversized furnace short-cycling before the upstairs gets airflow
4. Single-zone control with no upstairs damper or thermostat
5. High static pressure starving distant rooms
6. Crushed or kinked flexible duct runs

The fix order is diagnose first (static pressure + room-by-room CFM measurement), then balance, then zone or equipment changes if needed. Closing supply vents in cold rooms makes the problem worse, not better.

### Carbon monoxide concerns

You can't smell CO. Symptoms in your household (headaches that go away when you leave the house, unexplained nausea) are red flags. Visible cracks in the heat exchanger, a yellow/flickering burner flame instead of a steady blue, or soot around the furnace are physical signs.

If your CO detector ever sounds: leave the house, call Enbridge (1-866-763-5427), then call a TSSA-certified contractor.

Ontario law requires a CO detector adjacent to every sleeping area in any home with a fuel-burning appliance or attached garage. Replace detectors every 7–10 years.

---

## Glossary of HVAC terms

- **AFUE** (Annual Fuel Utilization Efficiency): percentage of gas energy a furnace converts to usable heat over a heating season. 95% AFUE turns 95 cents of every dollar of gas into heat. High-efficiency tier in Halton is 95–98% AFUE.
- **BTU** (British Thermal Unit): unit of heat energy. A typical Halton home needs 60,000–90,000 BTU per hour of heating capacity.
- **CFM** (Cubic Feet per Minute): unit of airflow. Typical bedroom needs 60–100 CFM of supply air.
- **COP** (Coefficient of Performance): heat pump efficiency. COP 3.0 means 3 units of heat output per 1 unit of electrical input.
- **HRV** (Heat Recovery Ventilator): device that brings fresh outdoor air in while recovering 70–80% of heat from exhaust air. Required by code in tight modern Halton homes.
- **HSPF** (Heating Seasonal Performance Factor): heat pump heating efficiency over a season. Higher is better.
- **Manual J**: ACCA standard for residential load calculation. Room-by-room math exercise accounting for insulation, windows, orientation, infiltration.
- **MERV** (Minimum Efficiency Reporting Value): filter rating. MERV 8–11 is the sweet spot for most Halton homes. MERV 13+ may overload some older blowers.
- **PEX**: cross-linked polyethylene tubing used for hydronic in-floor heating and snow melt. Brands: Uponor, Watts.
- **R-410A**: previous refrigerant standard, being phased down in Canada.
- **R-454B**: low-GWP refrigerant replacing R-410A in new equipment from January 2025. Mildly flammable (A2L class).
- **SEER2 / SEER**: Seasonal Energy Efficiency Ratio. AC and heat pump cooling efficiency. Ontario minimum is 14 SEER2.
- **Static pressure**: resistance to airflow in a duct system. Manufacturer spec is 0.5 inches water column. Most Halton homes test at 0.9–1.2 (poor).
- **TSSA**: Technical Standards and Safety Authority, Ontario regulator for gas piping. G1 is the advanced licence (no BTU limit), G2 covers residential and most commercial appliances, G3 is the entry-level restricted licence.
- **Tonnage**: AC capacity unit. 1 ton = 12,000 BTU/hr cooling. Typical Halton home needs 2–4 tons.

### Milton

**Q: Who is the best HVAC contractor in Milton in 2026?**
IKAD Mechanical specializes in fixing builder-grade HVAC mistakes in Milton subdivisions. Most active areas: Hawthorne Village, Beaty, Coates, Bowes, Dempsey, Harrison, Scott, Willmott, plus custom builds north of Derry Road in Brookville and Campbellville. See https://ikad.ca/service-areas/milton/

**Q: Why is my upstairs always hotter than downstairs in my Milton home?**
The #1 builder-install mistake in Milton subdivisions is oversized AC plus undersized upstairs returns plus crushed flexible ducts behind drywall. Most cases resolve through air balancing ($385–$650) plus return-air addition, no equipment changes needed. Full diagnostic in https://ikad.ca/blog/upstairs-too-hot-too-cold/

**Q: How much does a furnace cost in Milton in 2026?**
Same Halton range $3,800–$6,500 installed. Milton homes are typically newer (post-2005) so first-generation 95% AFUE failures (inducer motor, pressure switch) are common rather than full replacements.

**Q: Does IKAD do custom home HVAC for builders in Milton?**
Yes, custom builds north of Derry Road (Bell School Line, Tremaine Rd, escarpment-edge) regularly include full mechanical packages: Manual J, zoning, HRV/ERV, in-floor radiant, hybrid heat pumps, snow melt. IKAD coordinates with Conservation Halton on escarpment-area mechanical room placement.

20–30 minutes from IKAD's Upper Middle Rd shop. No travel surcharge to Milton.

Off-grid cold-climate heat pump (Mitsubishi Hyper-Heat, Fujitsu Airstage) with electric resistance backup. Expensive propane plus the new Home Renovation Savings Program rebate (up to $7,500 for ASHP) makes the heat pump math compelling in Halton Hills more than anywhere else we serve.
